affiliations.date_precision: Formal resignation effective August 1942; active Marine duty began June 1941, so end of day-to-day college work is not established
affiliations.research_notes: The Echo records a formal resignation effective August 1942 while Eddy had been on Marine active duty since 1941. The 1989 Marine history describes the active-duty transition in June 1941. These are overlapping formal title and service dates, not proof of continued day-to-day college employment.

affiliations.role_title: Marine officer and Naval Attaché in Cairo, then Tangier
affiliations.date_precision: Active-duty orders effective June 1941; Cairo attaché posting by about August 1941; Tangier by January 1942; commission continued alongside COI and OSS roles
affiliations.research_notes: The Cairo naval-attaché posting immediately preceded Eddy's COI transfer. Marine status continued in parallel, so it is not counted as the sole immediate affiliation before OSS's June 1942 creation.

affiliations.date_precision: January 1942 Tangier arrival is documented; June 1942 marks agency succession, not a proven personnel-transfer day
affiliations.research_notes: Mattingly's Marine Corps history says Donovan transferred Eddy from the Cairo attaché posting to COI leadership in North Africa by January 1942. NARA dates OSS's succession to COI to 13 June 1942. Administrative paperwork for Eddy's exact OSS transition has not been reviewed.

claims.claim_text: Hobart and William Smith Colleges was Eddy's last documented civilian employer before his June 1941 return to Marine active duty. His formal presidency ended in August 1942.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Resignation, tendered because of the pressure of duty with the United States Marines, takes effect in August, 1942.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The contemporary Echo identifies Eddy as college president, states that he had served on Marine active duty since 1941, and dates his formal resignation to August 1942. The Marine history places his active-duty orders in June 1941.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High: exact full name, college presidency, Marine service, and indexed Colonel rank agree across institutional and military sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: Last civilian employer before active Marine duty is strongly date-bounded; formal title and military service overlapped. The precise last day of active college work is unknown.
claims.match_notes: Do not treat the August 1942 resignation as proof Eddy was still working day-to-day at the college after June 1941, and do not treat Hobart as his immediate COI or OSS predecessor.

sources.locator_override: Chapter II, printed pages 25-26; June 1941 Marine active-duty transition

claims.claim_text: Eddy returned to Marine active duty in June 1941 and served as Naval Attaché in Cairo before Donovan assigned him to COI work in North Africa.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Marine Corps history traces June 1941 active-duty orders, a Cairo attaché posting about two months later, and Donovan's transfer of Eddy to the COI North Africa assignment by January 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High: exact indexed name and Colonel rank, distinctive presidency and wartime North Africa role.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Cairo military assignment predates the COI assignment; continued Marine status is concurrent with COI and later OSS work.
claims.match_notes: This corrects an earlier qualified immediate-Marine label; military status and intelligence-agency assignment were not mutually exclusive.

claims.claim_text: The best-documented institutional affiliation immediately before OSS's June 1942 creation was Eddy's assignment as Donovan's Coordinator of Information representative in North Africa.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A Marine Corps history documents Eddy's transfer from the Cairo naval-attaché posting to Donovan's COI North Africa operation by January 1942; NARA identifies OSS as the June 1942 successor to COI.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High: name, indexed Colonel rank, Hobart presidency, Marine service, and North Africa assignment corroborate the same individual.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded agency succession, but no personnel order establishing Eddy's individual administrative OSS transition date has been inspected.
claims.match_notes: COI, not Hobart, was the immediate institutional predecessor to the OSS organization. Marine commission continued concurrently. The source does not establish an exact OSS transfer day.
